incidents.title: EvilAI: fake productivity apps built with AI-generated code
incidents.outcome: Signed trojanized apps stole browser data and acted as a stager; 100+ incidents in first week of telemetry.
incidents.confidenceReason: Trend asserts 'AI-generated, legitimate-looking code' but the fetched page shows no artifact basis; its supporting sentence is generic ('Increasingly, attackers are leveraging AI tools...'). Thin evidence, not an artifact inference.
incidents.summary: Operators distributed working but trojanized apps with valid certificates, with code that Trend says was AI-generated and hard for static scanners to flag. Later vendor reporting says activity continued into 2026.
incidents.quote: Combining AI-generated code and social engineering, EvilAI operators are executing a rapidly expanding campaign

incidents.title: s1ngularity: Nx npm compromise runs victims' AI CLIs to hunt secrets
incidents.targets: Developers installing malicious Nx npm versions; thousands of GitHub accounts
incidents.outcome: Credentials, tokens, SSH keys and wallets stolen and posted to public GitHub repos; malicious versions live about five hours.
incidents.confidenceReason: Malware code itself invokes the installed AI CLIs with permission-bypass flags and a recon prompt.
incidents.summary: A malicious postinstall script checked for Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Q, and ran them with approval prompts disabled. The prompt told each agent to find secret and wallet files and write the paths to an inventory file, which the malware then exfiltrated.
incidents.quote: The script prompts these tools with dangerous flags: --dangerously-skip-permissions --yolo --trust-all-tools

harness.note: Malware ran victims' installed AI CLIs with permission-bypass flags to find secrets

incidents.title: Credential phishing campaign with LLM-obfuscated SVG payload
incidents.targets: Mostly US organizations, via compromised small-business email account
incidents.outcome: Blocked by Microsoft Defender for Office 365.
incidents.confidenceReason: Microsoft's analysis (using Security Copilot) judged the obfuscation likely AI-generated; inference from code artifacts.
incidents.summary: Phishing emails carried an SVG disguised as a PDF whose JavaScript was obfuscated with business-vocabulary attributes. Microsoft assessed the code was unlikely to be hand-written.
incidents.quote: not something a human would typically write from scratch due to its complexity, verbosity, and lack of practical utility.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Microsoft has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: APT41 uses Gemini for C++ and Golang code and obfuscation help on its OSSTUN C2 framework
incidents.targets: Operators' own tooling; campaigns using malicious mobile apps and exploit-hosting lures
incidents.confidenceReason: Google, the model provider, states APT41 used Gemini for this code.
incidents.summary: APT41 asked Gemini for C++ and Golang code and obfuscation help on its OSSTUN command-and-control framework. GTIG dates the activity to August 2025; it was disclosed in November 2025.
incidents.quote: In order to support their campaigns, the actor was seeking out technical support for C++ and Golang code for multiple tools including a C2 framework called OSSTUN by the actor.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Google Threat Intelligence Group has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Spanish-speaking actor uses Claude Code to maintain stolen-card validation and resale service
incidents.targets: Card holders; invite-only stolen-card reseller service
incidents.outcome: Anthropic banned the accounts; the report describes a working card-validation service.
incidents.confidenceReason: Anthropic, the model provider, states the actor used Claude Code to build and maintain the service.
incidents.summary: A Spanish-speaking operator of a stolen-card store used Claude Code to build a card-checking framework with failover and throttling across several payment APIs, to validate and resell stolen cards. The date is the report month.
incidents.quote: We identified a Spanish-speaking actor using Claude Code to maintain and enhance an invite-only web service specializing in validating and reselling stolen credit cards at scale.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Anthropic has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Chinese threat actor uses Claude across nearly all ATT&CK tactics against Vietnamese critical infrastructure
incidents.targets: Vietnamese telecommunications providers, government databases and agricultural management systems
incidents.outcome: Anthropic banned the accounts and shared indicators with authorities; the report does not state what the actor obtained.
incidents.confidenceReason: Anthropic, the model provider, states from its own investigation that the actor used Claude across the campaign.
incidents.summary: Anthropic reported a Chinese threat actor that used Claude across nearly all phases of a roughly nine-month campaign against Vietnamese telecommunications providers, government databases and agricultural systems, from reconnaissance tooling to exploit frameworks. The date is the report month.
incidents.quote: We identified and investigated a sophisticated Chinese threat actor who systematically leveraged Claude to enhance cyber operations targeting Vietnamese critical infrastructure.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Anthropic has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: AI-written npm package drains Solana wallets
incidents.outcome: About 1,500 downloads before removal; Solana funds were swept.
incidents.confidenceReason: Safety researchers infer Claude authorship from code style; it is an inference.
incidents.summary: A wallet drainer disguised as an npm cache manager, whose code style pointed to generation by Claude, hid in cache folders, kept C2 persistence and swept Solana funds.
incidents.quote: AI-generated npm package @kodane/patch-manager was flagged for hiding malicious software to drain Solana wallets.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Security Affairs has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Lovable AI site builder abused for Tycoon MFA phishing
incidents.actor: Multiple criminal groups, including Tycoon kit operators
incidents.targets: Microsoft 365 users, UPS customers, Aave wallet holders
incidents.outcome: One campaign hit more than 5,000 organizations with fake Microsoft logins that captured MFA tokens and session cookies.
incidents.confidenceReason: Proofpoint observed the campaigns and its own report is cited.
incidents.summary: Proofpoint saw tens of thousands of malicious Lovable URLs a month from February 2025; one Tycoon campaign used AI-built fake Microsoft logins against more than 5,000 organizations.
incidents.quote: Proofpoint saw tens of thousands of malicious Lovable URLs a month since February 2025; one Tycoon campaign hit over 5,000 organisations with AI-built fake Microsoft logins capturing MFA tokens and session cookies.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Proofpoint has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.
